$sequence.rationale: List likely runtime files, search for the governed batch dispatch action, inspect symbols, and find references before narrowing into source context.
Use the first batch to narrow into nearby implementation context, verify exact in-file matches with bounded file.search, and read the key files before summarizing.
The broad and narrow exploration batches are enough for the fixture run; summarize the bounded dispatch behavior.

code_dynamic_summarizer.summary: Fixture dynamic exploration completed: the model selected a bounded read-only tool batch, and AIR executed only declared tools under capability, budget, and repeated-call checks.

relevant_files.reason: Defines governed dynamic dispatch actions as part of the AIR IR.
Executes model-selected tool batches through the same governed path as static tool_call.
Verifies dynamic dispatch inputs, outputs, timeouts, retries, bounds, and approval-path requirements.

findings.title: Dynamic tool batches stay inside AIR contracts
findings.evidence: tool_batch_dispatch accepts typed {tool, input} choices, but runtime still rejects undeclared tools, mismatched capabilities, over-budget calls, repeated identical calls, schema-invalid outputs, and unsafe phase writes.

next_steps: Use this pattern to replace fixed read-only gathering stages with a bounded plan-act-observe batch loop.
Let the model start with repo.files/repo.search/repo.symbols before narrowing into repo.context or file.read_many.
Keep write tools out of dynamic dispatch until a module has an explicit approval path and narrow patch policy.
